Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 35, verses 1–2:

(p-4971) Surat Fatir

It is so named because of what it contains about the creation of the angels and their being possessed of wings varying in number, which indicates the wondrous craftsmanship of Allah, exalted is He, and the dazzling power of His ability.

Al-Muhayimi said: It is named so because it includes an explanation of the detailed nature of their message (risalah), in terms of their receiving the overflow (al-faydh) from Allah and conveying it to His creation, in one, two, three or more respects.

This indicates that the general message is for them; if it is like this, then how of the particular message, such as the sending down of the Qur'an? So it is possible that it has many aspects.

It has been narrated that Jibril had six hundred wings. End of quotation.

This surah is also called Surat (Fatir) because of the mention of this glorious name and beautiful attribute at its beginning. This surah is the conclusion of the surahs that open with praise (al-hamd), in which the four blessings are detailed, which are the comprehensive blessings. For the blessings of Allah, exalted is He, are of two kinds: immediate (ajilah) and deferred (ajilah, al-ajilah being the immediate) ... namely, the immediate is existence and continuance, and the deferred is likewise: origination once and perpetuation another time. As al-Razi explained.

(p-4972) In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate

Discussion on the interpretation of His, exalted is He, saying:

[1–2] "All praise is for Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, who made the angels messengers having wings, two and three and four. He adds to creation what He wills. Indeed, Allah is competent over all things. Whatever Allah grants to people of mercy, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release after Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise." [Fatir: 1–2]

"All praise is for Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth": that is, the Initiator and Innovator of them without precedent of example or material. "Who made the angels messengers having wings, two and three and four": that is, possessing wings in multiple numbers, varying in number according to the variation of their ranks, by which they descend, ascend, or hasten.

In the Sahih: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw Jibril, peace be upon him, on the night of the Isra', and he had six hundred wings." For this reason He, glorified is He, said: "He adds to creation what He wills": that is, He adds to the creation of wings and other things what He wills, of what His wisdom requires. "Indeed, Allah is competent over all things." "Whatever Allah grants to people of mercy" [Fatir: 2]: that is, a blessing, whether heavenly or earthly. "None can withhold it" [Fatir: 2]: that is, no one is able to withhold it. "And whatever He withholds, none can release after Him" [Fatir: 2]: that is, after His withholding. "And He is the Exalted in Might" [Fatir: 2]: the Overpowering over all that He wills. "The Wise" [Fatir: 2]: that is, in His command and His craftsmanship.

The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 35, verse 3:

(p-4973) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[3] ﴿O mankind, remember the favour of Allah upon you. Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the sky and the earth? There is no deity except Him, so how are you turned away?﴾

﴿O mankind, remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾ means: so that you may use it as evidence for His oneness in His divinity, because He alone is the one who sends it down, and it is not valid for the one who alone bestows blessings to have anyone associated with Him, for that is ingratitude toward Him which necessitates His anger. This is what He indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the sky and the earth?﴾, that is, the rain and the plants. ﴿There is no deity except Him, so how are you turned away?﴾, that is, you are diverted from the obligatory tawhid (for it is the requirement of thanking for blessings) to polytheism (shirk) and disbelief (kufr).

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[4] ﴿And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then already were messengers denied before you. And to Allah are returned all matters.﴾

﴿And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then already were messengers denied before you. And to Allah are returned all matters.﴾ So He will requite the one who denies, and his faction, with disgrace and the manifestation of the truth against them.

The discussion of the words of His saying, exalted is He:

[5] ﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is true, so let not the worldly life delude you, and let not the Deceiver delude you concerning Allah.﴾

﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is true﴾ — that is, what He has promised of His recompense: reward if you are sincere in following (the Prophet), and punishment if you disobey. ﴿So let not the worldly life delude you﴾ — that is, let not the enjoyment of it and the pleasure of its benefits distract you from working for the Hereafter and seeking what is with Allah. ﴿And let not the Deceiver delude you concerning Allah﴾ — that is, Satan (al-Shaytan). It has also been read with a ḍammah (al-Gharūr, as a noun meaning "the deceit/the great deceiver").

(p-٤٩٧٤) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[ 6 ] ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party so that they may be among the companions of the Blaze.﴾

﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party so that they may be among the companions of the Blaze.﴾ That is: by following desire and inclining toward this world.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 35, verses 7–8:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[7–8] ﴿Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment, and those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ ﴿Is one to whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive, so he sees it as good, [equal to one guided]? For indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So let not your soul be consumed with regret over them. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.﴾ [Fatir: 8].

﴿Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment, and those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ ﴿Is one to whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive, so he sees it as good?﴾ [Fatir: 8] That is: whoever has his evil deed made appealing to him, such that his desire overcomes his intellect, until his judgment is overturned, so he sees falsehood as truth and ugliness as beauty, is he like one who has not had it made attractive to him, but rather recognizes the truth and distinguishes the good from the evil? The answer has been omitted, owing to the indication of His saying: ﴿For indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾ [Fatir: 8], meaning: faith and following the truth. It is also permissible that its implied content is: "Is one to whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive [like one who is guided]? ... his soul would have gone out in regret over them," by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So let not your soul go out in regret over them, [in successive sorrows]﴾ [Fatir: 8], meaning: do not destroy yourself with grief over their misguidance and their failure to follow you. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾ [Fatir: 8], meaning: He will recompense them for it.

[7–8] ﴿Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment, and those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ ﴿Is one to whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive, so he sees it as good, [equal to one guided]? (p-4975)The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted:

[9] ﴿And it is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, and We drive them to a dead land and bring forth thereby life to the earth after its death. Such is the resurrection.﴾

﴿And it is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, and We drive them to a dead land and bring forth thereby life to the earth after its death. Such is the resurrection.﴾ That is: like the giving of life to the dead is the giving of life to the dead (the resurrection). Very often, may He be exalted, uses as evidence for the Return (al-ma'ad) His giving life to the earth after its death, so that the doubter may take heed in this matter, for it is among the most manifest and clearest of the signs.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[10] ﴿Whoever desires honor—to Allah belongs all honor. To Him ascends the good word, and righteous deed raises it. As for those who plot evil deeds, for them is a severe punishment, and the plotting of those will come to nothing.﴾

﴿Whoever desires honor﴾, i.e., nobility and exaltation: ﴿to Allah belongs all honor﴾, i.e., let him seek it from Him, by following His law (shari'ah), by loyalty to His prophets and messengers, by emulating them in righteousness and reform, in patience and steadfastness, and by casting off every reproach, out of desire for the truth and acting with sincerity. This is like the verse: ﴿Do they seek honor from them? Indeed, honor belongs entirely to Allah﴾ [al-Nisa': 139], and like the verse: ﴿Honor belongs to Allah, to His Messenger, and to the believers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8].

﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾, and it is the one who calls to the truth and reform, and who points out the paths of misguidance and corruption. ﴿And righteous deed raises it﴾, i.e., the righteous deed raises the good word. This is on the understanding that the pronoun in "it" refers to the good word, indicating that deeds are not accepted except with a word that is effective in conveying the call to good. The hidden pronoun refers to the deed, and the explicit one to the word; i.e., the righteous deed becomes the cause of its elevation and acceptance, because it actualizes and confirms it, as Allah the Exalted said concerning Shu'ayb, peace be upon him: ﴿I do not intend to oppose you in that which I forbid you. I intend only reform, as much as I am able﴾ [Hud: 88].

﴿And those who plot evil deeds﴾, i.e., the evil deeds that corrupt the welfare of the community and the building up of its civilization: ﴿for them is a severe punishment, and the plotting of those will come to nothing﴾, i.e., it will perish, because the truth prevails and nothing prevails over it.

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[11] ﴿And Allah created you from dust, then from a drop of semen, then He made you into pairs. No female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge. And no one is granted a lifespan, nor is any of his life shortened, except that it is in a Record. Indeed, that is easy for Allah.﴾

﴿And Allah created you from dust, then from a drop of semen, then He made you into pairs﴾ i.e., males and females, out of His kindness and mercy. ﴿No female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge. And no one is granted a lifespan﴾ i.e., of anyone. It is called "granted a lifespan" (mu'ammar) because of what it turns out to be; i.e., and no one's life is extended: ﴿nor is any of his life shortened, except that it is in a Record﴾ and this is His knowledge, Exalted is He, which preceded, by the arrival of its origin at it: ﴿Indeed, that is easy for Allah﴾ i.e., preserving, increasing, or decreasing is easy, because of the comprehensiveness of His knowledge and the generality of His power.

A subtle point:

The pronoun in ("his life" ['umurihi]) refers to the one granted a lifespan mentioned before it, in consideration of the original form from which it was transformed, since the original is: "and no one of anyone is granted a lifespan," as we mentioned; or it is by the well-known looseness in this, trusting that its interpretation will be grasped by the listeners, like their saying: "He owes me a dirham and its half," i.e., half of another dirham. Or the pronoun refers to the one whose life is shortened, not to the one granted a lifespan, as in the previous opinion; and although it is not explicitly stated in the ruling about the one mentioned, as it is said: "And by their opposites things become clear." So the pronoun returns to what is known from the context. Some of them have spoken at length on this, and its summary, as al-Shihab mentioned, is that there has been disagreement about the meaning of "granted a lifespan" [mu'ammar]. It was said: the intended meaning is his lifespan, as evidenced by what is contrasted with it in His saying: "is shortened" etc. It was also said: the one to whom a lifespan is given. And is this one person or two persons? According to the second view, it is one person. They said, for example: his lifespan is written as one hundred, then beneath it is written: one day has passed, two days have passed, and so on. So the writing of the original is the granting of a lifespan, and the writing after that is the shortening. As it is said:

"Your life is breaths that are counted; each time a breath of it passes, you have lost a part of it."

The pronoun in ("his life"), in that case, refers to the one mentioned, and the one granted a lifespan is the one for whom God has made a lifespan, whether long or short. According to the first view, it is two persons: the one granted a lifespan is the one whose lifespan is increased, and the pronoun then refers to "another one granted a lifespan," since what is added to one's lifespan is not what is shortened from one's lifespan. This is the view of al-Farra' and some grammarians, and it is an instance of істихдам (istikhdam, a figure in which one word carries two meanings), or something similar to it. End of quotation.

Then Exalted is He pointed to other signs of His power and oneness, with His saying:

The discussion of the Exalted's saying:

[12] ﴿And the two seas are not alike: this one is sweet, fresh, pleasant to drink, and that one is salty, bitter. And from each you eat fresh flesh, and you extract ornaments that you wear. And you see the ships therein plowing through, that you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful.﴾

﴿And the two seas are not alike: this one is sweet, fresh﴾ — i.e., exceedingly sweet. ﴿Pleasant to drink⁠—its drink is wholesome⁠—and that one is salty, bitter﴾ — i.e., intensely salty. ﴿And from each you eat fresh flesh﴾ — meaning fish. ﴿And you extract ornaments that you wear﴾ — i.e., adornment with which you beautify yourselves. As the Exalted said: ﴿From both of them come forth pearls and coral﴾ [al-Rahman: 22]. ﴿And you see the ships therein plowing through﴾ — i.e., they cut through the water and split it with their passage. ﴿That you may seek of His bounty﴾ — i.e., by travelling in them. ﴿And perhaps you will be grateful﴾.

(p-4978) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[13] ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. And those you invoke instead of Him do not possess even a thin membrane on a date pit.﴾

﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term﴾ meaning: for the duration of its orbit, or its end point, or the Day of Resurrection. ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. And those you invoke instead of Him do not possess even a thin membrane on a date pit﴾, i.e., how then could they deserve worship? (Al-qitmir) is the thin membrane wrapping the date stone, and it is a proverb for paucity and insignificance.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[14] ﴿If you call upon them, they will not hear your call; and even if they heard, they would not respond to you. And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association of them (with Allah). And none can inform you like one who is (completely) Aware.﴾

﴿If you call upon them, they will not hear your call﴾ because they are inanimate objects. ﴿And even if they heard﴾ — i.e., hypothetically — ﴿they would not respond to you﴾ — i.e., because they have no power to benefit. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association of them﴾ — i.e., they will acknowledge its falsehood and that they have no authority in it. ﴿And none can inform you like one who is (completely) Aware﴾ — i.e., no informant can inform you of the matter like a great Aware One who has informed you of it, namely the Truth, glorified is He, for He is the Aware of the reality of affairs, unlike all other informants. The purpose is to confirm what He has informed of concerning the state of their gods, and to negate what they claim for them of divinity.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 35, verse 15:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted:

[15] ﴿O mankind, you are the poor toward Allah, and Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.﴾

﴿O mankind, you are the poor toward Allah﴾, i.e., [in need of] His mercy, His care, His kindness, and His provision at every moment and every breath. The connection of this verse with what precedes it, which is the mockery of the rivals (andad), is to remind them of turning to Him, may He be exalted, and of supplication and entreaty to Him when harm touches them and misfortune grips their throats. Indeed, they feel within themselves a compelling impulse to ask of Him that cannot be turned back, and a driving urge to take refuge in Him that nothing can repel. As He has explained in more than one verse, this indicates that He, may He be exalted, is the one truly deserving of worship, owing to His absolute self-sufficiency, as He said: ﴿And Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy﴾, i.e., the one praised for His blessings, which cannot be counted.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[16–17] ﴿If He wills, He can remove you and bring a new creation.﴾ ﴿And that is not difficult for Allah.﴾ [Fatir: 16–17]

That is: not impossible for Him. Al-Zamakhshari said: This is a threat against them, because of their taking rivals to Him, their disbelief in His signs, and their disobedience, as He said: ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people other than you﴾ [Muhammad: 38].

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[16–17] ﴿If He wills, He can remove you and bring a new creation.﴾ ﴿And that is not difficult for Allah.﴾ [Fatir: 16–17]

That is: not impossible for Him. Al-Zamakhshari said: This is a threat against them, because of their taking rivals to Him, their disbelief in His signs, and their disobedience, as He said: ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people other than you﴾ [Muhammad: 38].

The discussion of the Lord's words, the Exalted:

﴿No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another.  And if a heavily laden soul calls out for help with its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if it is a near relative. You can only warn those who fear their Lord in the unseen and establish the prayer. Whoever purifies himself, purifies only for his own soul. And to God is the final return.﴾

﴿No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾, meaning: no sinful soul shall bear ﴿the burden of another﴾, that is, the sin of another soul. Rather, it bears only its own burden, which it has committed. No soul is seized for the sin of another soul, as the tyrants of the world seize the guardian for the ward and the neighbour for the neighbour. There is no conflict with the verse ﴿And they will surely bear their burdens, and burdens along with their burdens﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 13], because it concerns the misguided who misguide others: they bear the burdens of misleading people along with the burdens of their own misguidance. All of that is their own burdens; there is nothing in it of the burden of others.

(p-4980) ﴿And if a heavily laden soul calls out﴾, meaning: a soul whose sins have weighed it down, ﴿for help with its load﴾, meaning: calls for someone to carry some of its burdens so that it may be lightened, ﴿nothing of it will be carried﴾, meaning: it will not be answered, and it will not be relieved by the carrying of anything. ﴿Even if it is a near relative﴾, meaning: even if the one called upon, as implied by the call, is a relative of the caller, whether a father, a son, or a brother. This cuts off the hopes of those who expect benefit from their kinship and from the help of those close to them, and it shows that no soul can own anything for another soul, and that every person is held in pledge for what he has earned.

Then He explained who takes heed and remembers. He, glorified is He, said: ﴿You can only warn those who fear their Lord in the unseen and establish the prayer. Whoever purifies himself﴾, meaning: cleanses himself of the filth of sins, ﴿purifies only for his own soul. And to God is the final return.﴾

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[19] ﴿And the blind and the seeing are not equal﴾.

﴿And the blind and the seeing are not equal﴾ is a parable for the disbeliever and the believer.

The commentary on His saying, may He be exalted:

[20] ﴿Nor are the darknesses and the light﴾.

﴿Nor are the darknesses and the light﴾ is a parable for truth and falsehood.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 35, verse 21:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[21] ﴿Nor is the shade and nor is the scorching heat.﴾

﴿Nor is the shade and nor is the scorching heat﴾ is a parable for reward and punishment. And ﴿al-harur﴾ (the scorching heat) is the hot wind at night, though it may also occur by day.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[22] ﴿And the living and the dead are not alike. Indeed, Allah causes whom He wills to hear, but you cannot make those in the graves hear.﴾

﴿And the living and the dead are not alike﴾ is another parable for the believers and the disbelievers. That is: the living of heart through faith in Allah and His Messenger, and knowledge of His revelation, are not alike to the dead of heart, because disbelief has overpowered them until they no longer comprehend from Allah His command and His prohibition, nor recognize guidance from misguidance. ﴿Indeed, Allah causes whom He wills to hear﴾ means: He grants him success in understanding His signs and in being admonished by His admonitions. ﴿But you cannot make those in the graves hear﴾ means: just as one cannot make those in the graves hear the Book of Allah so that He guides them by it to the path of right guidance, likewise one cannot make benefit from the admonitions of Allah and the clarification of His proofs one whose heart is dead to the knowledge of Allah, the understanding of His Book, and the clear proofs. This is a reinforcement of the parable of those who persist in disbelief with the dead, and an elaboration on the despair (of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him) regarding their faith.

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[23] ﴿You are but a warner.﴾

﴿You are but a warner﴾, meaning: your only duty is to convey and to warn. If the one warned is among those who listen to the warning, it benefits him; and if he is among the stubborn, then you bear no responsibility for him.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 35, verse 24:

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[24] ﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And there is no nation but that a warner has passed among them.﴾

﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And there is no nation but that a warner has passed among them.﴾ That is: there is no nation of the nations that adhere to a religion (millah) except that a warner has passed among them before you, warning them against their disbelief in Allah and removing their excuses (ilal). As He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide﴾ [al-Ra'd: 7], and as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid Taghut." Among them were those whom Allah guided, and among them were those upon whom error was justified﴾ [al-Nahl: 36].

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[25] ﴿And if they deny you, those before them also denied; their messengers came to them with clear proofs, and with the scriptures, and with the illuminating Book.﴾

﴿And if they deny you, those before them also denied; their messengers came to them with clear proofs, and with the scriptures, and with the illuminating Book.﴾ That is: and if they deny you and do not respond to you, then do not concern yourself with them, and take comfort in those messengers of earlier times who were denied. They came to their peoples with signs and manifest marvels as evidence of the soundness of their prophethood, with scriptures that guided them to the paths of success and prosperity, and with the illuminating Book, which, for whoever reflects upon it and contemplates it, proclaims that it is the truth speaking with rightness and sincerity. The meaning is not that every messenger came with all that is mentioned, such that each messenger would have to have a book; rather, the meaning is that some messengers came with this and others came with that. It is also permissible that the reference of the whole be to one thing, and the conjunction (waw) serves to indicate the difference of attributes.

Discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[26] ﴿Then I seized those who disbelieved, so how was My disapproval?﴾

﴿Then I seized those who disbelieved, so how was My disapproval?﴾ That is: My rejection (inkar) through punishment. In it there is further emphasis and a depiction of its terror.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 35, verse 27:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[27] ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth thereby fruits of varying colors? And among the mountains are tracts, white and red, of varying shades, and others intensely black.﴾ ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth thereby fruits of varying colors? And among the mountains are tracts, white and red, of varying shades, and others intensely black.﴾ The majority (al-Jumhur) read ﴿judad﴾ with a dammah on the jim and a fathah on the dal, the plural of (juddah) with a dammah, which means a path or streak, from (jaddahu), meaning when he cut it. That is: and among the mountains (p-4983) are those possessing streaks (dhawu judad), i.e., paths of white and red. The mudaf (the noun governed by the construct) was supposed to be implied, because the mountains are not themselves the streaks. Gharabib: the plural of (ghirbib), which is the intensely black, the one that is extremely black; it is said: "aswad ghirbib" (intensely black), just as it is said: "ahmar qani" (deep red) and "asfar faqi" (bright yellow), for emphasis. It has been placed first here, though by rights an emphasizing word should follow what it emphasizes, for intensity. Some scholars held that it is placed first by inversion (muqaddam min ta'khir), on the basis of the permissibility of placing the adjective before the noun it describes.

﴿And among mankind, beasts and cattle are those whose colours are varied. Likewise, only those of His servants who have knowledge fear God. Indeed, God is Mighty, Forgiving.﴾

The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

﴿And among mankind, beasts and cattle are those whose colours are varied, likewise﴾: that is, a variation like that, as in the variation of fruits and mountains. His words, may He be exalted, ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear God﴾, complete His words, may He be exalted, ﴿You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen﴾ [Fatir: 18], by specifying who among people fears Him, mighty and majestic, after explaining the differences in their classes and the variation in their ranks. As for the spiritual attributes, this is by way of illustration (tamthil), and as for the outward attributes, it is by way of explicit statement (tasrih), so that each of the two receives its due and fitting explanation. That is: only those who know Him, mighty and majestic, and what befits Him of His glorious attributes and beautiful acts, fear Him, exalted, unseen. This is because the basis of khashyah (fear born of awe) is knowledge of the One feared and awareness of His affairs. Whoever knows Him, exalted, fears Him more. As he, peace and blessings be upon him (ﷺ), said: "I am the one among you who fears God most, and the one among you who is most mindful of Him." For this reason, He follows it with mention of His acts that indicate the perfection of His power. Since the disbelievers are far removed from this knowledge, warning them entirely is ruled out. This is what Abu al-Su'ud conveyed.

Al-Qashani said: That is, none fears God except the knowing ones who recognise Him (al-'urafa'). This is because khashyah is not the fear of punishment; rather, it is a state in the heart of submissive humility and self-abasement upon conceiving the attribute of greatness and calling it to mind. Whoever does not conceive His greatness cannot fear Him. Whoever has God manifest to him in His greatness fears Him with the fear that is due to Him. Between the conceptual presence available to the knowing person who is not a gnostic, and the manifest vision that is firmly established for the gnostic knowing person, there is a vast distance. The degrees of khashyah cannot be counted, according to the degrees of knowledge and gnosis. End.

Some exegetes mention here the irregular reading (al-qira'a al-shadhdha) in which the divine name is in the nominative (raf'), and al-'ulama' (the knowing ones) is in the accusative (nasb), so that: "God's servants fear Him, the knowing ones." They interpret khashyah as "glorification" (ta'zim) by way of metaphor, and perhaps they cite the verse:

"I revere you out of reverence, though I have no power over you, but it is because the eye is filled with its beloved."

Al-Nashr (the book) has criticised this reading, and the truth is with him, because it contradicts the context (siyaq) and the preceding context (sibaq). How little the editors need to blacken pages with such irregular readings! And success is from God.

﴿Indeed, God is Mighty, Forgiving﴾: that is, He prevails over everything by His greatness, and forgives those who repent, turn back to Him, and do righteous deeds.

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[29] ﴿Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah, and establish the prayer, and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly, hoping for a commerce that will never perish.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah﴾, i.e., they persist in its recitation and reflection upon it, in order to act upon what is in it. ﴿And establish the prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly, hoping for a commerce that will never perish﴾, i.e., a reward and bounty that does not come to an end. The word "commerce" (tijarah) is a metaphor (isti'arah) for obtaining reward through obedience, and "perishing" (bawar), meaning slump and destruction, is a supporting element (tarshih) for the metaphor.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 35, verses 44–45:

(p-4989) The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[44–45] ﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them, though they were greater than them in strength? Allah is not to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on the earth. Indeed He is ever Knowing, Competent.﴾ ﴿And if Allah were to seize the people for what they have earned, He would not leave upon the earth [so much as] a creature crawling upon it. ﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them, though they were greater than them in strength? Allah is not to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on the earth. Indeed He is ever Knowing, Competent.﴾ ﴿And if Allah were to seize the people for what they have earned﴾ [Fatir: 45], i.e., for what they have committed of their sins: ﴿He would not leave upon its surface [so much as] a creature﴾ [Fatir: 45], i.e., a living being that crawls, because of the evil of their sins. The pronoun refers to the earth, since it was mentioned earlier. ﴿But He defers them to a specified term﴾ [Fatir: 45], i.e., He defers their punishment and their seizure for what they have earned until a known term with Him. ﴿And when their term comes, indeed Allah is ever Seeing of His servants﴾ [Fatir: 45], i.e., when the term of their punishment comes, indeed Allah is ever Seeing of His servants, of who deserves to be punished and who merits honour.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 35, verses 44–45:

(p-4989) The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[44–45] ﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them, though they were greater than them in strength? Allah is not to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on the earth. Indeed He is ever Knowing, Competent.﴾ ﴿And if Allah were to seize the people for what they have earned, He would not leave upon the earth [so much as] a creature crawling upon it. But He defers them to a specified term. And when their term comes, indeed Allah is ever Seeing of His servants.﴾ [Fatir: 45]
